resolution.note: hc host opens the successor through env -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION; open tests assert it; live hc probe (hc run ... env -u CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION bash -c 'env | grep -c ...') printed 0. Restarting herdr-core from a clean environment stays with the operator.

title: A successor opened through hc saves its transcript
body:
Source: operator question 2026-11-15 on the banner "Transcript saving is off — inherited CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION marker"
Why: the herdr-core server process carries CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION=1 (it was started from inside a Claude Code session), every hc terminal inherits it, so a successor lead opened through the hc host saves no transcript and krn ledger (which reads transcripts) loses its cost and outcome.
Outcome: the hc host starts the successor's shell without CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION (`env -u`), so the successor lead saves its transcript; restarting herdr-core from a clean environment stays an operator step.
Proof: hc host open test asserts the unset word; a live successor opened through hc shows no CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION in its environment.
